subject: Follow-up: Logging & redaction requirements / next steps

Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Logging & redaction requirements / next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the action items we agreed on: 

- Scope: FintechCo wants request/response logging for debugging and analytics, but any PII (names, emails, account numbers, SSNs, payment card numbers) must be redacted before being stored in long-term logs.
- Headers: strip or mask sensitive headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-Auth-Token) from both request and response logs.
- Trace IDs: you want some identifier for correlation in logs, but prefer these not to be raw request IDs that can be mapped back to customer records. We discussed truncated/hash approaches.
- Retention: target retention for detailed request/response payloads = 90 days; aggregated metrics can be retained longer.
- Hosted vs Private: FintechCo prefers hosted initially but may require Private deployment for full control over raw log retention.

Next steps (agreed):
1) Neha to send a short technical note on redaction/retention options and how we handle headers/trace IDs (we attached a one-pager).
2) FintechCo to share a small sample (sanitized) log set or example payloads to make sure our regex rules cover the fields you care about.
3) Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive next week with your security team (Laura/security@fintechco.com).

Attaching: redwood-logging-redaction-summary.pdf (summary of options and tradeoffs).

If I missed anything, please shout.

Best,

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Logging & redaction requirements / next steps — technical note

Hi Alex / team —

Quick technical notes on the redaction & logging options we discussed. Attaching a more formal spec (redaction_spec_v1.pdf) but here are the highlights: 

1) Redaction timing
- Hosted API: by default we redact at ingestion (streaming pipeline) — sensitive fields are removed/masked before persistent storage. Raw transient buffers are kept in ephemeral memory and not written to durable store. For customers requiring absolute proof, we can provide a SOC-style attestation and describe the pipeline flow.
- Private deployment: customers can choose to retain raw logs in their own S3/Blob storage; Redwood can then be configured to run redaction jobs before indexing or keep raw for a configurable retention window.

2) Redaction strategies supported
- Field-level regex rules (configurable per-customer) — e.g., credit_card: replace with "[REDACTED_CC]"; ssn regex -> "[REDACTED_SSN]".
- Token masking for conversational payloads (mask entire token spans flagged as PII).
- Header scrubbing: preconfigured list (Authorization, Cookie) + allowlist for required headers.
- Custom transforms: hash-only (SHA256 hex) or HMAC with customer-provided key for trace IDs. Hashing is irreversible; HMAC can be used if you want deterministic but not-plain IDs.

3) Trace ID handling (options)
- Truncated: store first 8 chars (useful for quick sanity checks) — low risk but reversible mapping if you have the original ID.
- Hash/HMAC: deterministic mapping without storing original value — supports correlation without exposing raw IDs.
- Reversible encryption: we can support reversible encryption for Private deployments where FintechCo manages the key. For hosted, reversible storage is not recommended for security posture but can be discussed under an enterprise contract.

4) Performance impact
- Runtime regex redaction on large JSON payloads can add 2-15ms p95 depending on payload size and rules. We mitigate with: streaming parsers, precompiled regex, and work off of hot-path config. For high-throughput customers we recommend prefix/KV caching + async redaction for non-blocking indexing.

5) Retention controls
- Configurable by data class: raw-ish request/response (redacted) retention default 90d; aggregated telemetry 13 months. We expose retention policies via per-tenant config and API.

6) Auditability
- We can produce redaction logs (audit trail of what rules were applied) without including raw payloads.

Next steps I recommend:
- FintechCo shares a 5-10 sample payloads (sanitized or with placeholders) so we can validate our regex rules.
- Security deep-dive (30m) where we can demo an ingestion+redaction flow and show live metrics.

Attachment: redaction_spec_v1.pdf (detailed rules & examples).

Happy to jump on the call — I can demo the HMAC vs hash behavior if helpful.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai

Alex — quick operational note from a pricing/throughput lens:
- If you require synchronous inline redaction on every request with multiple complex regex rules, there is a unit-cost and latency impact we should model. For the hosted offering we can include a "redaction complexity" tier in the proposal.
- For most customers we achieve the best tradeoff with streaming redaction + prefix caching. If FintechCo expects >2k rps of large payloads, let's quantify and I can put together an estimated cost delta.

Marissa, happy to include a short pricing appendix in the proposal once we get sample payloads.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
